prov.heading: Provision for Credit Losses
prov.text:
The provision for credit losses is charged to operations to adjust the ACL to a level deemed appropriate by management and is based upon the volume and type of lending the Bank conducts, industry standards, the amount of nonperforming loans, general economic conditions, particularly as they relate to its market area, economic forecasts, and other factors that may affect the ability to collect on the loans in its portfolio.

The Company recorded a provision recovery for credit losses on loans for the three months ended September 30, 2026 of $0.1 million compared to a provision of $11.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in the provision expense was primarily the result of $30.5 million of expense related to the asset resolution plan recorded in the second quarter of 2026. During the three months ended September 30, 2026, $3.2 million of net charge offs were recorded compared to $3.5 million during the three months ended September 30, 2025.

nonint.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonint.text:
The following table presents noninterest expense for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025.

Noninterest expense was $12.8 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026, a decrease from $25.2 million during the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in the third quarter of 2026, as compared to the third quarter of 2025, was primarily due to the third quarter 2025 restructuring expense of $7.3 million, and a decrease in compensation expense of $3.1 million.

Noninterest expense was $45.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, a decrease from $58.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 . The decrease was primarily the result of the third quarter 2025 restructuring expense of $7.3 million, a decrease in compensation expense of $8.1 million, partially offset by an increase in loan servicing and origination expense of $3.1 million.

nonop.heading: Noninterest Expense
nonop.text:
The following table presents noninterest expense for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025.

Noninterest expense was $12.8 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026, a decrease from $25.2 million during the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in the third quarter of 2026, as compared to the third quarter of 2025, was primarily due to the third quarter 2025 restructuring expense of $7.3 million, and a decrease in compensation expense of $3.1 million.

Noninterest expense was $45.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, a decrease from $58.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 . The decrease was primarily the result of the third quarter 2025 restructuring expense of $7.3 million, a decrease in compensation expense of $8.1 million, partially offset by an increase in loan servicing and origination expense of $3.1 million.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
Income tax benefit was $0.3 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase from income tax benefit of $7.1 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The change was attributed to a decrease in net loss.

Income tax benefit was $13.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, a decrease from income tax expense of $8.0 million for the nine ended September 30, 2025. The change was attributed to a higher net loss for the current year.

At September 30, 2026, the Company had $36.2 million federal net operating loss carryforward and $34.6 million of state net operating loss carryforward. At September 30, 2025, the Company had $7.3 million of federal net operating loss carryforward and $7.9 million of state net operating loss carryforward. The Company expects to fully utilize the net operating losses.

The effective income tax rate was 25.94% for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and 26.82% for the nine months ended September 30, 2025.

net.heading: Net Loss
net.text:
The Company had a net loss for the three months ended September 30, 2026 of $0.7 million, or $0.04 per common share and diluted common share, compared to net income for the three months ended September 30, 2025 of $19.1 million, or $4.71 per common and diluted common share. The change from the third quarter of 2025 was the due to decreases in provision for credit losses of $11.2 million and noninterest expense of $12.4 million, and an increase in noninterest income of $2.2 million, partially offset with a decrease in income tax benefit of $6.7 million.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company had a net loss of $39.3 million, or $3.76 per common share and diluted common share, a decrease from net loss of $21.9 million, or $5.57 per common share and diluted common share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The change was primarily due to decreases in net interest income of $4.6 million and noninterest income of $22.8 million and increases in provision for credit losses of $13.5 million and noninterest expense of $13.2 million, partially offset by income tax benefit of $5.7 million.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text: Net interest income was $10.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, a decrease from $11.3 million during the three months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease in net interest income during the third quarter of 2026, as compared to the year ago quarter, was mainly due to a decrease in loan interest income, including fees, of $4.8 million, partially offset by a decrease in interest expense on deposits of $3.1 million.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income (Loss)
Noninterest income.text:
The following table presents noninterest income (loss) for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025.

Noninterest income was $1.1 million during the three months ended September 30, 2026, an increase from a negative $1.1 million during the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in the third quarter of 2026, as compared to the third quarter of 2025, was the result of a third quarter 2025 fair value adjustment on loans held for sale of $5.1 million, partially offset by a decrease in gain on sale of government guaranteed loans of $3.0 million.

Noninterest income was a negative $4.8 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, a decrease from $17.9 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The decrease was primarily the result of a decrease in gain on sale of government guaranteed loans of $16.1 million, a decrease in government guaranteed loan fair value gains of $7.8 million, a decrease in government guaranteed loan packaging fees of $1.7 million and second quarter 2026 loss on nonmarketable equity securities of $1.5 million, partially offset by a 2025 fair value adjustment on loans held for sale of $5.1 million.

intro.text: BayFirst Financial Corp. is a bank holding company that operates through its wholly owned subsidiary, BayFirst National Bank (the “Bank”), together referred to as “the Company” or “BayFirst”. BayFirst commenced its bank holding company operations on September 1, 2000, by acquiring all shares of the Bank. BayFirst’s primary source of income is from the Bank, which serves a broad spectrum of consumers and small businesses in the Tampa Bay/Sarasota region. BayFirst strives to be a progressive institution in its products and services, technology, design, and social responsibility. As of December 31, 2025, BayFirst had consolidated total assets of $1.30 billion, total loans held for investment of $963.9 million, total deposits of $1.18 billion, and total shareholders’ equity of $87.6 million. BayFirst’s corporate office is located at the BayFirst Executive Center, 700 Central Avenue, St.
